name: Chatsworth House
scope: Main quadrangular house and connected north wing, courtyards, stone facades and roofline; exclude the separate stable block and gardens.
era: surviving exterior represented by selected dated references

review.method: Individually inspected six local Qualla originals, all four pages of the official 2026 visitor plan, Historic England architecture description and aerial roof context.
review.notes: Distinct west pediment, twelve-bay south front, ten-bay east front, bowed north range, open courtyard, lower attached north wing with skylights, orangery and tall open belvedere. Detached stables excluded.

candidates.caption: Chatsworth after its makeover

An oil painting showing the west front of Chatsworth House in the 18th century, painted by William Marlow (1740–1813). The stable block is to the left of the house and the cascade to the right. The north wing had not been built. This picture emphasises the romantic aspect of Chatsworth's setting on the edge of the Peak District. The hills behind house were windswept moorland when it was built. They were not forested until the 18th century, and are still partially exposed in this view.
Chatsworth Christmas Market

This engraving by Kip and Knyff shows Chatsworth House part way through the 1st Duke's alterations. The south front has been rebuilt but the original east front survives. The baroque garden has been laid out, but only the first, smaller version of the Cascade has been built, and the Canal Pond hasn't been dug. The 1st Duke's stables are to the left of the house.
